title: Causal Intervention at the Training Stage: Does Reducing RLHF Reward for Agreement Reduce Sycophancy?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core finding that modifying RLHF reward signals reduces sycophancy has been established by multiple groups (linear probe penalties, agreement signal subtraction, DPO with sycophancy-labelled pairs). Replicating this on Llama 3.1 8B adds limited new insight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning Llama 3.1 8B with a modified RLHF reward function requires significant ML engineering expertise: reward model training, PPO implementation, and evaluating on sycophancy benchmarks. Far beyond beginner CS students even with mentorship. Medium compute may be insufficient for RLHF training loops.

narrow_scope.reasoning: RLHF pipeline setup, reward function modification, training, and evaluation across two benchmark suites is a substantial multi-week project. Even scoped to a single model, the infrastructure requirements push well beyond 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple published works directly address this question. Shapira et al. (2026, 'How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy') derive the unique policy minimizing KL divergence to standard RLHF subject to a sycophancy constraint. Burns et al. (2024, 'Linear Probe Penalties Reduce LLM Sycophancy', arxiv 2412.00967) use linear probes to penalize sycophancy markers in the reward model and demonstrate successful reduction across multiple open-source LLMs. DPO-based approaches with sycophancy-labelled pairs also show significant reduction. The specific intervention (modifying RLHF reward to subtract agreement signal) has been demonstrated experimentally under best-of-N optimization. The core research question is answered.
